summary: The bill requires the Interior Secretary to reissue within 60 days the November 2020 regulation that removes the gray wolf from Endangered Species Act protections and bars judicial review of that action.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to reissue a specific regulatory action under the Endangered Species Act. It contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, budgets, or expenditures.
The bill addresses only the regulatory status of gray wolves under the ESA and has no tax-related provisions.
No connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The legislation is unrelated to firearms or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions concerning immigration, borders, or citizenship.
The bill does not address reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No military, defense, or national security spending elements are present.

The bill mandates reissuance of a rule delisting the gray wolf from ESA protections and shields that action from judicial review. This directly reduces the scope of an environmental protection statute, aligning with the direction of limiting environmental regulations.
No welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs are addressed.
The bill contains nothing related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions exist.
The legislation does not touch sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization measures are included.
The bill has no fiscal or deficit implications.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
No election administration, voting access, or election-integrity measures are present.
The legislation is silent on technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No labor, union, or workplace-protection provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
